newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Goldfields sees A$20-25 mln profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Goldfields sees A$20-25 mln profit.

text.p: Goldfields Ltd said on Wednesday it has lowered its forecast for its net profit for the 1996/97 year to between A$20 and A$25 million due to higher exploration, operating and interest costs.
The company had previously forecast a net profit of A$30 to A$46 million.
Goldfields, about 57 percent owned by RGC Ltd, was created last year to combined the gold assets of Pancontinental Mining and RGC after RGC's takeover of Pancon.
The company is one of Australia's top six gold producers.
Goldfields earlier announced a net profit after abnormals of A$14.19 million for 1995/96.

It said the lower 1996/97 profit forecast was due to higher than expected operating costs at the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea, higher exploration spending and a higher capital spending programme and poorer operational results at the Paddington gold mine.

Goldfields said that in 1995/96 a strong performance at the Kundana mine in Western Australia, exploration successes in Tasmania and Western Australia, and good progress at the Henty gold project in Tasmania were balanced by operating difficulties at Paddington and Porgera.

The profit result was adversely impaced by the low plant availability experienced during commissioning of the Stage III plant upgrade at Paddington and by operating difficulties at Porgera, of which it owns 25 percent.
Porgera contributed a profit of A$38.4 million to Goldfields in 1995/96, down from A$44 million in 1994/95.
The reduced profit level was a direct result of total gold production at 834,060 ounces, being seven percent lower than 1994/95.
